svg.title: Time to answer 1, 10 or 50 questions about one document
svg.desc: Median seconds for each system, for documents of 3,000 and 6,000 tokens, on a log axis; the table in the report has every value.
svg.text: Time to answer 1, 10 or 50 questions about one document
Median seconds over 5 to 10 documents per point; log scale. RTX PRO 6000 at 600 W, each system on its own server, on two boxes (see the notes).
One request: document read once for all questions
One request: document read again for every question
One request per question: document shared by the prefix cache
Hollow ring: measured on the 2026-10-09 box, a slower clock (see the notes)

svg.text: decisio, H2O-Lightning-4B, Jeff-1.0-Large and Quyet-1.0-Large were measured in one session on one box on 2026-10-11 (RTX PRO 6000 at 600 W, AMD EPYC 9374F; SM clock p50 2,220 to 2,610 MHz).
Kev, Blink, Torchcast, Perplexity and deck31b were measured on the 2026-10-09 box (about 1,570 MHz under its 600 W cap), so their figures are the slower-clocked ones; they are hollow rings.
A dot is the median wall time to answer every question about one document: one request that carries them, or the requests in a row for the systems that take one question each.
decisio runs in its served default mode. Jeff-1.0-Large and Quyet-1.0-Large read the document again for every question; Jeff takes up to 8,192 tokens and Quyet 6,000 (both ran at 3,000 and 6,000).
Torchcast reads a shared beginning of 4,096 tokens or more once per request, so at 6,000 tokens it does not re-read the whole document.
